headline: Bangladesh crushes Australia for historic first Test win on Australian soil
summary: The Tigers defeated a full-strength Australia by nine wickets in Darwin, becoming the quickest Asian team to win a Test Down Under in just their third attempt.
details: Bangladesh made history in Darwin, securing their first-ever Test win on Australian soil by crushing the hosts by nine wickets on Sunday. The Tigers needed just 57 runs after bowling Australia out for 284, wrapping up proceedings swiftly on Day 4.

This monumental victory makes Bangladesh the quickest Asian team to win a Test in Australia, achieving the feat in their third Test Down Under. They surpassed Pakistan (7 Tests) and India (12 Tests) in this regard.

Only England and South Africa have won their first Test in Australia sooner or as quickly, respectively. This nine-wicket triumph is Bangladesh's second-biggest Test victory by wickets, following their 10-wicket win over Pakistan in 2024.

The win marks only Bangladesh's second Test victory over Australia in seven encounters, with the first being in Mirpur in 2017. It also signifies Australia's first home Test loss to an Asian team other than India in 31 years.
This is Bangladesh's second Test win in SENA (South Africa, England, New Zealand, Australia) countries, building on their famous victory against New Zealand in Mount Maunganui in 2022.
Pacer Hasan Mahmud delivered an outstanding performance with match figures of 9-111, the second-best by a Bangladesh pacer in Tests and the best by a Bangladesh bowler outside the country.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto recorded his third away Test win, making him the most successful Bangladesh captain in away Tests. He also holds the record for most Test wins overall as captain, with nine.
The Darwin Test saw a record attendance of 18,352 fans, the highest ever at the venue, witnessing this historic moment for Bangladesh cricket.

headline: Storm risk of 60 km/h in several districts by morning
summary: A storm with winds up to 60 km/h is forecast to hit several districts across Bangladesh by morning. Residents are advised to stay updated on weather warnings.
details: A storm with wind speeds reaching up to 60 kilometers per hour is anticipated to affect several districts in Bangladesh. The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has issued a warning for these areas.
The storm is expected to develop and impact the affected regions by morning. Authorities are urging residents to remain vigilant and follow official advisories.
